title: add strict JSON Schema response_format with streaming validation and OpenAI compat mapping
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: Add first-class support for a strict JSON Schema style 'response_format' that can be validated synchronously or during streaming, and ensure OpenAI compatibility layer maps its 'response_format' and 'schema' usage into our runtime behavior. This PR introduces a 'strict' validation mode that rejects outputs that do not conform and produces clear, machine-readable error messages for callers. It also adds incremental/streaming validation so that long-running generation can be validated as tokens arrive and early failures can be surfaced to clients.

What changed (summary): implemented a response_format parser that accepts 'json_schema' payloads and a 'strict' flag; added streaming validator that emits validation events on the stream (prefix event type: validation_error / validation_warning); updated the OpenAI compatibility shim to translate OpenAI-style 'response_format' and 'schema' into our internal representation; added runtime guards so fallbacks to permissive mode are available via policy for backward compatibility; extended API docs and SDK examples to show the new flags.

Key behaviors: in strict mode the runtime will attempt to fully validate the completed JSON object against the schema; if validation fails the request returns a structured 400-level error with a short machine code (e.g. VALIDATION_ERROR_SCHEMA_MISMATCH) and a human message that includes the top 3 violations. When streaming, partial validation runs on complete JSON fragments; streaming validation failures are emitted inline as 'validation_error' events and, if strict mode is enabled, the stream is closed with a trailing error event. The OpenAI compat layer accepts both top-level 'response_format' and the legacy 'schema' key and preserves the strictness flag (openai: "response_format": {"type":"json_schema","strict":true}).

Compatibility: default behavior remains permissive unless the caller sets strict mode. For customers relying on older OpenAI-compatible behaviors we added a rollout toggle (policy: openai_compat.strict_response_format=false) that keeps the legacy permissive semantics. We added a migration note in docs for Dedicated/Private admins.

Testing and rollout: unit tests cover schema parsing, validator edge cases, and error formatting. Integration tests exercise streaming validation with large token sequences and function-calling scenarios. We staged the change behind a feature flag and ran a canary on 5% of traffic for 48h before enabling broadly.

Docs: API reference updated with examples for strict mode, streaming validation event types, and sample SDK usage.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the validation engine pluggable; future work will add optional remediation suggestions (e.g., 'coerce_number') and richer error paths for tool-calling workflows.

review_comments: Liam Ortega: Requesting clarification on the streaming semantics: when exactly do we emit validation_warning vs validation_error? Please add a compact state machine comment in stream_validator.go.

Author (Priya Nair): Added state machine comment and unit tests for boundary chunking in stream_validator.go. validation_warning is emitted for recoverable/formatting issues that do not break the final schema; validation_error is emitted for violations that would make final validation fail under strict mode.

Mina Chen: Found an edge case where function-calling outputs (tool responses) may include top-level non-JSON tokens (e.g., plain text). We should ensure tool output is passed through permissive parsing unless the tool contract specifies JSON. Recommend updating the docstring and adding a test.
Author: Added guard and test to ensure tool outputs are treated as permissive by default; added docstring to function-calling plumbing.
Carlos Duarte: CI flaked once on e2e streaming run; re-ran and all checks are green. LGTM after minor comment fixes.
Liam Ortega: Approved and merging via squash once canary validated.
release_notes: Add support for 'json_schema' response_format with optional 'strict' validation mode and streaming validation events; OpenAI compatibility shim maps legacy fields to this behavior. Default remains permissive.
testing_notes: Ran: unit test suite for validation engine (200+ cases), streaming integration with 3 different chunk sizes, canary at 5% traffic for 48h, OpenAI-compat regression tests against legacy clients. Added fuzz tests for schema edge cases (missing required fields, extra properties, type coercion scenarios).
implementation_notes:
- response_format parser normalizes OpenAI and Redwood schemas into an internal 'SchemaDescriptor' string token list.
- stream_validator runs incremental JSON parsing using a safe tokenizer; emits events to the stream layer using existing event envelope ('event.type' set to validation_error/validation_warning).
- In strict mode final validation uses ajv-compatible rules ported to Go; errors are summarized to top 3 entries to avoid large payloads.
- OpenAI compat adapter maps legacy 'schema' into response_format and preserves 'strict' boolean when present; policy gate 'openai_compat.strict_response_format' defaults to true for new installs and false for older clusters.
- Kept validation engine pluggable: interface validators.Validator -> implemented JSONSchemaValidator and NoopValidator.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Strict mode could break clients that expect permissive output. Mitigation: gated by explicit 'strict' flag and policy toggle for OpenAI compat; rollout via canary and observability dashboards added (metric: schema_validation.failure_rate). Risk: streaming validation may add CPU overhead. Mitigation: incremental checks are cheap and we added a tunable sampling rate and max-validation-size config.
changelog_entry: response_format: support for JSON Schema with 'strict' validation mode and streaming validation events (validation_error/validation_warning); OpenAI compat maps legacy schema to new response_format.
